blocks.text: This connects back to recapping drift detection, already covered in this topic. A genuinely deployed model's own weights genuinely stay completely frozen, already covered generally in Inference.
The genuinely real world it operates in genuinely keeps changing, gradually making that frozen snapshot genuinely less accurate, the exact underlying cause explored throughout the rest of this topic.

blocks.text: This connects back to collecting fresh training data, already covered in this topic. Genuinely retraining entirely from scratch genuinely uses the fresh data alongside the original historical dataset.

Genuinely fine-tuning instead genuinely starts from the existing deployed model, already covered generally in Full Fine-Tuning, a genuinely important choice explored throughout the rest of this topic.

blocks.text: This connects back to retraining from scratch versus fine-tuning, already covered in this topic. A genuinely newly retrained model genuinely gets evaluated carefully before it ever genuinely replaces the currently live one.
This genuinely prevents a genuinely worse model from accidentally replacing a genuinely working one, a genuinely essential safety step explored throughout the rest of this topic.

10. Worked Example
The example below directly demonstrates validating a retrained model against the currently live model, already covered in this topic, before deciding whether to replace it.

code.content:
def evaluate_model(model_weights, validation_data):
    # already covered as validating before replacing the live model in this topic
    total_error = 0.0
    for input_value, true_output in validation_data:
        prediction = input_value * model_weights["scale"] + model_weights["bias"]
        total_error += abs(prediction - true_output)
    return total_error / len(validation_data)

live_model = {"scale": 1.4, "bias": 0.3}  # already covered as the currently live model in this topic
retrained_model = {"scale": 1.52, "bias": 0.18}  # already covered as a freshly retrained model in this topic

# already covered as collecting fresh training data, used here for validation, in this topic
validation_data = [(1.0, 1.7), (2.0, 3.1), (3.0, 4.6), (4.0, 6.0)]

live_error = evaluate_model(live_model, validation_data)
retrained_error = evaluate_model(retrained_model, validation_data)

print(f"Live model average error (already covered in this topic): {live_error:.4f}")
print(f"Retrained model average error: {retrained_error:.4f}")

# already covered as validating before replacing the live model in this topic
if retrained_error < live_error:
    print("\nRetrained model genuinely performs better: deploying to replace the live model")
else:
    print("\nRetrained model genuinely performs worse: rejected, live model stays unchanged")
